_note: The KNOWN-GAP allowlist for ElementParityTest.kt (OpenSource/Engine/Android/render). A fixture whose tag is listed under `missing`, `module`, or `dclass` is REPORTED, not failed, when :render has no ElementSpec for it — this is how CI stays green while the implementation waves close the gaps. `partial` suppresses (but still reports) a NAMED mismatch key (`attributes.<name>` / `geometry.<name>` / `colors.<name>` / `aliases`) for an element that IS implemented — use it only for divergences pinned in a .kt header. Shrink this file as waves land: an empty file = full enforcement. A registered ElementSpec is ALWAYS enforced against its fixture, even if its tag is (stale-)listed here.
_missing_note: Godot is demand-driven (no <Godot/> tag anywhere in the .dsx corpus, `godot` ios-only in the platform map) — it lands with the first customer demand, not a parity wave.

module._note: Implemented on Android by a module android/ facet's ComposeStackComponents registration — outside :render's test classpath, so the JVM parity test cannot load their specs. Their parity is owned by the module header + device QA.

dclass._note: iOS-only by decision (android-status.md section 3) — never expected to grow an Android spec.

pager.attributes.bind: iOS bind= is the data-bound page list plus one row template. Android bind= is an alias of value= (the page index); data-bound pages ride list registration, not bind=. Pinned in the StackNodeView.kt Pager header.
